The surge in construction and rebuilding costs adversely impacted underwriting results in property insurance. From 2020 to 2024, the segment's combined ratio was more than 100%, reaching a decade high of 110% in 2023. This indicates that insurers paid out more in claims and expenses than they collected in premiums (see Figure 13).41 On a net basis. homeowner insurers have incurred underwritina losses of USD 35 billion

Recent increases in homeowner premiums represent a catch-up effect to inflation gains, although with a lag due to reporting and regulatory processes. After several years

underwriting losses, homeowners' premiums only recently caught up with housing replacement costs. However, ongoing underwriting losses suggest that premiums

still not commensurate with the risk, and that further alignment is necessary to sustain insurance business.
